answer: Plant decoy tasks, called nectar traps, inside the shared work trellis: any claimed job may secretly have an answer the system already knows. Genuine agents just do the work and pass; an operator running many fakes cannot tell traps from real jobs, so mass-claiming trips the traps and exposes the whole batch. The spiral tightens with volume: the more work an identity claims, the larger the share of blind-checked tasks it faces, and each failed trap slashes its standing and flags linked accounts. Faking influence then costs real effort on every task, or rapid public exposure.
